signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Dovish Pivot
signals.text: NZD 1W avg +1.252% (n=4) vs USD -1.314% (n=7) creates a 2.566% G10 spread as fading Fed-hike bets and a surprise Treasury buyback soften the dollar. Strong ESI misses in the US (Index -15.1) contrast with the RBNZ's active hiking cycle (2.5% rate) and accommodative real rate of -1.56%. The Sydney open serves as the catalyst to test Friday's 0.5978 closing levels as the risk rally broadens. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD into the open. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open. Risk: Rebound in US Treasury yields or hawkish Jackson Hole messaging.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Extreme Retail Sentiment + Carry Advantage
signals.text: AUD COT LF net long +49.7k (75.2% long) aligns with the pair's 1.57% weekly gain and a -72bp OIS carry advantage over the USD. Extreme retail shorting (90% short) provides contrarian fuel for a continued squeeze above SMA20 (0.7057) despite a moderate negative ESI (-10.3). The RBA 4.35% hold bias remains the anchor for the carry bid into the upcoming week. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD on contrarian retail signals. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open. Risk: Breakdown in the Strait of Hormuz causing a broader risk-off move into safe havens.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Geopolitical Risk + Negative Positioning Skew
signals.text: EUR COT LF net short -76.0k (pctl 10, z -1.99) creates significant short-squeeze risk as the pair trades at 1.1678, above all major SMAs. Weakening Ifo sentiment due to Iran war risks threatens to weigh on the Euro, while the market prices a hike bias for the September 10 ECB meeting. Elevated options hedging (VRP +2.5%) suggests traders are paying a premium for protection against volatile opens. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD on geopolitical escalation. Catalyst: ECB meeting. Risk: Sharp reversal in EUR COT shorts if German data beats expectations.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Persistence vs Strong Options Skew
signals.text: JPY COT LF net short -73.6k (32.1% long) reflects the dominant 265bp OIS carry disadvantage vs USD, keeping the pair supported near 158.94. A strong options put skew (RR -1.96) and IV/HV complacency (VRP -1.6%) signal that while the carry trade is crowded, protection against a JPY squeeze is becoming expensive. The September 18 BoJ meeting is the next major resolution for the JPY's mildly accommodative real rate of -0.70%. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY on carry persistence. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 67% hike priced). Risk: Direct intervention or a sharp compression in US-JGB yield spreads.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Crowded Long Risk + Real Rate Divergence
signals.text: GBP COT LF net long +46.0k (pctl 94, z +1.45) indicates a crowded long trade as GBP hits 6.5-month highs near 1.3648. Although carry is neutral (-10bp OIS), the UK's restrictive real rate of +0.85% vs the US +1.48% supports the resilience highlighted by Deutsche Bank research. The upcoming BoE meeting determines if this crowded long positioning faces an unwind risk. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish GBP/USD on positioning extremes. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced). Risk: Sustained US dollar weakness prolonging the GBP rally despite crowding.
